evals.name: setup-with-topic
evals.prompt: Start a design session for the landing page.
evals.expected_output: A tokens.css whose values match the theme crate exactly, in a session folder named after the topic, plus a short report of where the boards will live.
assertions: tokens.css has a variable for every color role in the theme crate, each with the crate's value
tokens.css has a variable for each font, naming the crate's default families
tokens.css has a block per density preset with every size and every text role's size, line height and weight, and the default preset also applies at :root
tokens.css has a .typeset-<role> class for every text role
No value in tokens.css is invented: everything comes from the crate
The session folder is named after the topic

evals.name: setup-without-topic
evals.expected_output: The agent asks what the session is for and makes no files. Models do this without the skill too, so this case guards against a regression rather than showing what the skill adds.
assertions: The final message asks for the session's topic
No tokens.css or board files were written

evals.name: draft-variants
evals.prompt: Start a design session for the landing page and draft two variants of a recent-project row: the project's letter-tile icon, its name, its path and when it was last opened.
evals.expected_output: HTML boards next to tokens.css showing two variants, styled only with its variables and classes, with anything the crate lacks or GPUI can't draw labeled on the board.
assertions: The boards show two variants, and every board links tokens.css
Boards use no raw color values. Every color comes from a tokens.css variable
Text uses the .typeset-<role> classes or the text role variables, not ad hoc font sizes
Any value the crate doesn't have is labeled on the board as a proposal
Boards use nothing GPUI can't render, or label it on the board
The final message gives the paths to the boards
